## Motivation

Multimodal cache equality must depend on actual model-facing content, not a short scalar or a caller-provided hint. The old GPU reduction admits structured collisions, composite keys lose information through `hash(tuple(...))`, and matching only part of a media placeholder can still reuse unrelated KV state.

This is a correctness-first fix across the shared VLM paths, not a model-specific opt-in or a universal speedup claim.

## Modifications

- Add shared CPU/GPU BLAKE3-256 with typed shape/dtype/container/metadata identities. GPU tensors transfer only their digests to the host.
- Preserve full identities through embedding caching, batch deduplication, sessions, EPD and native Rust sidecars. Rust output digests use full SHA-256 and bind the serving configuration at ingress.
- Namespace KV requests using ordered full media identities and `cache_salt`. Short or partial placeholder matches cannot substitute for complete identity equality.
- Stop allowing caller `mm_hashes` to override content identity, including precomputed embeddings. Keep the separate explicit `--trust-mm-content-hashes` boundary documented.
- Preserve Kimi source/config/grid protections; cover composite processors and finalized OCR metadata. Reuse full Qwen/Muse artifact fingerprints on cache hits instead of rehashing their feature tensors.
- Add common-contract, kernel, native/transport and real Qwen input regressions, plus documentation of compatibility and prefix-sharing tradeoffs.

The GPU BLAKE3 kernel is adapted from @xupinjie's #46028; author credit is preserved. Related narrower work: #44653, #46552, #46815 and #47066. This PR does not modify diffusion conditioning caches or include #37537.

## Accuracy Tests

Current conflict-resolution head `16b61eade952` normally merges pinned main `133f712a498e`. It preserves main's move of multimodal wire types into `managers/req_types.py` and relocates the complete strong-identity implementation there, without duplicate classes or an eager scheduler/identity import. Full BLAKE3 and typed-identity hashing remain unchanged from the preceding PR head.

Exact-head validation on an isolated B300 (driver 590.48.01, PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130, Transformers 5.19.0) passed:

- CPU-hidden identity/padding/cache and native Rust contracts: **114 tests + 81 subtests**, with one CUDA-only test skipped.
- GPU hash/IPC/request/abort contracts: **97 tests + 187 subtests**, no skips.
- GPU-visible identity tests plus the previously skipped cache case: **18 tests + 26 subtests**, no skips; 17 cases repeat CPU-covered tests in the GPU-visible environment.

All final phase exits were 0; changed-file pre-commit and scoped relocation checks passed. The first CPU-hidden attempt failed collection because an existing test helper indexes an empty `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES`; rerunning the same source with an out-of-range GPU ordinal and an explicit zero-device assertion passed. IPC teardown emitted a producer-lifetime warning; ending GPU memory/utilization were 0 MiB/0%. This is conflict-integration validation, not a new full-model, performance, multi-node or leak-free-soak claim. Current-head targeted CI is requested separately.

Previous delivery head `48150838db03` normally merges the pinned main commit containing #47835, fixing the two unrelated diffusion fixtures from the old CI snapshot. It preserves @g0djan's #47066 diagnostic-checksum fix and leaves full BLAKE3/typed VLM identity unchanged. Isolated B200 validation on this exact head passed **244 tests + 241 subtests**, exit 0: hash/identity (28 + 197 subtests), request/abort/Rust interface contracts (103 + 44 subtests), and four diffusion fixture/cache files (113). Runtime imports and freshly built extensions used this checkout; driver 580.126.09, PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130. This is merge-integration validation, not a new full-model serving or performance result.

Remote H200 validation, implementation `15884434708` (the following commit changes documentation only):

- **976 passed**, 23 skipped, 149 passing subtests: common CPU/processor/cache/session/encoder tests, including actual Python and Rust radix trees.
- **51 passed**, 133 passing subtests: GPU hash/IPC/VMM/encoder tests. One FABRIC test fails because this container returns `CUDA_ERROR_NOT_PERMITTED`; POSIX fallback passes. The test is unchanged and normally runs on GB300.
- **2 passed**: native Rust encoded-sidecar tests. Native Python/Rust suite: 49 passed plus four PIL resize parity subtest failures reproduced on the pristine base; no tolerances or assertions changed.
- Real Qwen2.5-VL-3B: CPU and CUDA IPC, videos with caches enabled/disabled, raw/processor/precomputed inputs, A-B-A and concurrent isolation. Final existing input fixture: **4 passed**.

- Real InternVL3.5-1B: **22 requests passed**. This is representative E2E coverage, not a claim that every VLM checkpoint was tested.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 224 image | 40.62-40.70 | 41.47 | 21.83-21.85 | 22.18 |
| 1024 image | 68.26-68.82 | 72.67 | 29.55-29.81 | 29.63 |
| Shared 2048-token text + 224 image | 41.07-41.14 | 42.66 | 22.44-22.74 | 22.74 |

- [x] Changed-file pre-commit checks, including Rust format/clippy
- [x] Regression tests and representative real-model validation
- [x] Documentation, caller trust boundaries and performance tradeoffs
- [ ] Upstream CI
